newsitem.title: USA: Small investors in U.S. hold mixed view of future.
newsitem.headline: Small investors in U.S. hold mixed view of future.

text.p: U.S. investors happily see a bright financial future for themselves but worry that both the U.S. government and the U.S. economy will fail them, according to a survey released on Tuesday.
Seven out of 10 investors, defined as people with $10,000 or more in equities, mutual funds or other financial assets, believe they will meet their financial goals in the next year.
Some 74 percent see themselves meeting their financial goals within five years, according to a Gallup Organization poll commissioned by the Paine Webber Inc brokerage.

But 54 percent of the 1,000 American investors polled doubted the federal government would end government overspending or hammer out financial fixes for Social Security and other benefit programs widely seen as ailing.
Women investors are less optimistic than men, Paine Webber Senior Vice President Louis Poulin said a news conference here.

The poll, which Gallup and Paine Webber plan to conduct every three months, also showed that investors in Miami were substantially more optimisic than investors in New York, Los Angeles, Chicago and Dallas.
In the five cities targeted in the national poll, Miami was some 18 percent above the national mean in bright personal financial expectations. Dallas was 19 percent below the national norm.
Miami investors were the least pessimistic about government resolving its issues, while those in Dallas were the most optmistic.
New Yorkers were the least optimstic about their personal finacial prospects among the five cities, according to the poll.
